description: Definitive Expo/React Native standards for robust, performant, maintainable cross-platform apps.

Structure: maintain a clean, scalable project structure.
`assets/`: static assets (images, fonts).
`src/`: application logic:
`src/components/` reusable UI; `src/screens/` top-level views; `src/navigation/` navigation when not using Expo Router's `app/`; `src/hooks/` custom Hooks; `src/utils/` utilities/constants; `src/services/` API clients/data fetching.
Directories: `kebab-case`; components: `PascalCase`; hooks/utils: `camelCase`; variables/functions: `camelCase`; global constants: `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`.

Always use functional components. Prioritize TypeScript and clear styling. All new code must be in TypeScript. Centralize styles with `StyleSheet` for readability/performance.

Use file-based routing with the `app/` directory. ❌ BAD: Manual stack/tab navigator setup in a single file for all routes.

Always create new objects/arrays when updating state; update immutably. Carefully manage `useEffect` dependency arrays to prevent unnecessary re-renders or infinite loops.

Use `.env` files with `EXPO_PUBLIC_` for client-side variables. ❌ BAD: `API_KEY=mysecret` in `.env` and `process.env.API_KEY`. (Exposed in bundle, not automatically injected)
Never store sensitive keys (e.g., private API keys) in `EXPO_PUBLIC_` variables. They are bundled client-side. Use EAS Secrets for server-side secrets.

Use `React.memo` for pure functional components when props are unchanged. Memoize functions/values passed to `React.memo` components or expensive computations with `useCallback` and `useMemo`. For large apps, lazy load screens with `React.lazy` and `Suspense`.

Handle potential errors in asynchronous code with `try/catch`. Use a global Error Boundary to catch UI errors in React components.

Test component logic and user interactions with Jest & React Testing Library; aim for ≥80% coverage. ❌ BAD: No tests, or only shallow rendering tests. Use snapshot testing for UI components to detect unintended changes.
